title: The deer and the fire-sticks
hook: a deer runs off with a brahmin's fire-sticks, the Pandavas chase it to save his sacred fire, and a voice at a lake says: answer first
carry: agni carries the offering to the gods

segments.voice: Yesterday: vara, a boon. Savitri talked with Death until he gave Satyavan back, and women still keep Vat Savitri for her. Your line was a vrat offers your fast for another's long life.
screen: `VARA, A BOON FROM DEATH.` · `A VRAT FOR ANOTHER'S LIFE.`

segments.voice: A pair of fire-sticks, swinging from a deer's antlers. A brahmin comes running to the Pandavas in their forest exile. He had left his arani, the two pieces of wood he rubs together to kindle his sacred fire, hanging on a tree. A deer rubbed against the tree, the sticks caught in its antlers, and now it's bounding away with them. Without them, he can't keep his fire. The five brothers take up their bows and go after it, deeper into the trees than any of them meant to go.
screen: `FIRE-STICKS ON A DEER'S ANTLERS.` → `A BRAHMIN'S FIRE AT STAKE.` → `FIVE BROTHERS GIVE CHASE.`

segments.voice: Why would five princes risk their lives for two sticks of wood? Because of what the sticks make. In the Vedas, Agni, the god of fire, is the messenger who carries offerings up to the gods. A Vedic householder kept a sacred fire, and kindled it by rubbing the arani together. Without them, the brahmin can't kindle his sacred fire, his line to the gods. Protecting it is a king's dharma, so the brothers run. And that fire is still at the center of Hindu life. At a wedding the couple walk around a fire, with Agni as their witness. When a family moves into a new home, a priest often lights a havan in the living room. But the deer stays just out of reach. They shoot and miss, and it's gone. Parched, they sink down under a tree, and Yudhishthira sends Nakula to climb it and look for water. Nakula sees green plants and cranes, and goes alone. He finds a lake, clear and still. He is about to drink when a voice speaks from nowhere. Don't be rash, child. This lake is mine. Answer my questions first, then drink. Nakula is burning with thirst. He kneels, drinks, and falls down dead on the bank. The questions haven't been asked yet.
screen: `AGNI, MESSENGER TO THE GODS.` · `FIRE AT THE HEART OF HINDU LIFE.` · `THE DEER ESCAPES. NAKULA SEEKS WATER.` · then, large: `HE DRINKS, AND FALLS.`

segments.voice: If you have a diya or a candle, light it and set it where you can see it; if not, picture one. Watch the flame for a few breaths. Many Hindu homes light a lamp like this every morning or evening. Think of one thing you'd like to offer today: a kind word, an hour of work, a meal shared. If you pray, offer it into the flame in your own words; if not, simply set your intention by the light.
Arani, the fire-sticks that kindle a sacred fire, carried off on a deer's antlers. Five brothers chase them for a brahmin's fire, and one brother drinks before he listens. Today's word.
Your line: agni carries the offering to the gods. Two sticks of wood, and five brothers ran for them. Until tomorrow.

screen: `DAY 801 COUNTS.` → `TOMORROW: FOUR BROTHERS AT THE LAKE.`

chat.meaning: The Pandavas risked everything to win back a brahmin's fire-sticks, because his sacred fire was his line to the gods. In a havan, Agni carries the offerings up, so a new home starts with fire.

arani.meaning: two pieces of wood rubbed together to kindle a sacred fire

brahmin.meaning: a member of the priestly class

Nakula.meaning: one of the twin Pandava brothers

Yudhishthira.meaning: eldest of the five Pandava brothers

Agni.meaning: the god of fire, who carries offerings to the gods

havan.meaning: a fire offering of ghee and grain, often at a new home or a rite

recall: a wager, a stake in the dice game

sources.ref: Mahabharata, Vana Parva (Aranyaka Parva), the episode of the Yaksha's questions: the brahmin's arani carried off by a deer; the chase; the brothers' talk under the tree; Nakula at the lake
